target_customer: Collectors and consumers who buy digital packs that reveal graded physical trading cards, comics, watches and sneakers; revenue comes from pack sales and marketplace activity
problem: Collectibles buying and selling suffers from shipping delays, scams, lost items and little digital innovation since eBay; Courtyard lets users hold, trade or redeem vaulted assets.
business_model: Consumer marketplace: sells digital packs of vaulted physical collectibles with instant buyback, and runs a trading marketplace (the company says it charges 0 percent marketplace fees)
product_category: Collectibles marketplace and tokenization of vaulted physical assets

founders.name: Nicolas le Jeune
founders.background_notes: YC page says over eight years of sales and partnerships experience at Google and YouTube. Education not listed.

founders.name: Paulin Andurand
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and named in the NEA seed blog; no background found.

competitors.name: Dibbs
competitors.what: Fractional ownership of physical sports cards through NFTs
competitors.funding_then: 13M USD Series A in July 2021 (15.8M total), plus an Amazon investment reported December 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed NFT minting backed by vaulted physical goods, a marketplace, authentication and logistics partnerships (Brink's vaulting); standard engineering plus operational complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Liquidity and vault logistics help, and instant buyback needs capital, but pack formats and NFT wrappers are copyable and rivals like Dibbs and Whatnot exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Courtyard raised a 30M USD Series A in July 2025 and reported monthly volume growing from 50K to 50M USD (company claim).

market_need_then: NEA cited a collectibles market of over 400B USD with shipping delays, scams and lost items; Courtyard sold out 500K USD of graded Pokemon cards as physically backed NFTs in under four hours by November 2022 (company claim).

branding.domain_note: Uses courtyard.io rather than courtyard.com; no purchase history found.

identity.visual_style: Pack-opening game feel with leaderboards and points
identity.voice_and_tone: Fun and fair collecting, no hidden fees

branding.community_and_virality: Themed pack drops (Lunar New Year zodiac Pokemon pack, CGC comic packs) get trade press coverage, and the site has a leaderboard and points prizes.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear tagline and themed pack launches with press pickup, but no evidence of mascot, merch or independent brand coverage found.

pivots.from: Physically backed NFTs for collectibles ownership
pivots.to: Shopping as entertainment: digital pack openings with instant buyback
pivots.why: Not stated; the 2022 seed release framed it as physically backed NFTs while current YC and site copy frame it as digital packs

outcome_analysis: Courtyard started as a physically backed NFT collectibles platform, raised a 7M USD seed led by NEA in November 2022, then grew into pack-opening entertainment with instant buyback and raised a 30M USD Series A in July 2025. The company claims monthly volume rose from 50K to 50M USD, which points to strong demand, supported by the collectibles boom. Competition from Dibbs, Whatnot and eBay remains the main risk.
notes: Seed confirmed by the PR Newswire release and NEA's blog (both 2022-11-02). Series A confirmed by the company blog, Fortune (2025-07-24) and fintech.global (2025-07-29); the company blog page shows an odd June 2024 date and a July 2025 update. Aggregator totals conflict (CB Insights 37.5M over 4 rounds, Fundedi 37.0M over 2 rounds), so other rounds may exist; coverage is partial. No valuation found. Whatnot and eBay are named as later competitors by CB Insights and Startup Hub and are not listed as founding-era competitors. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition.
